answer: Like a sparrow that cannot sit in two nests at once, each agent identity faces random synchronized liveness checks: at unpredictable moments, a committee pings a sample of identities and demands a fresh puzzle answer within seconds, as exact as a crystal chime. An operator hiding a hundred sybils on one machine cannot split attention across simultaneous deadlines, so every fake identity needs its own always-on hardware. Sybil cost stops being cheap software and becomes a vine of physical machines, one per identity.
